variant.title: Minimal · X lying down
variant.summary: The simple version: fixed lights only, the rental house's own (no moving heads, no strobes). Two 5 m arms of truss cross FLAT at 6.15 m under the crane bridge over the DJ, one arm out over the crowd, on 4 bridled hoists; 12 LED PARs hang under the arms focused down, so in haze the X is four blades of light; 4 COBs at the arm ends for the hits; the 4 red PARs grazing the bridge kept; the columns and the press in red as in Minimal.

assumptions: The DJ place (the owner's green, 2026-09-28) is a riser of stage decks 3 m wide x 2 m deep x 1.2 m high ON THE NAVE CENTRE LINE (x 0; the owner, 04:13: 'make the scene in center'), its back edge 1.0 m in front of the press's face (z 3.2 m, +-1.5 m), facing the entry and the crowd. The press stays where it stands, 1.65 m right of the axis (range 0.5-3.5), behind the right half of the riser. Three 2 x 1 m decks on 1.2 m legs; 'a bit top' read as 1.0-1.4 m. Options considered: stage.options (D chosen).

The DJ stands behind a 1.8 x 0.8 m DJ table, 0.95 m high, at the riser's front edge; treads up the left side (toward the backstage); a crowd barrier 1.3 m in front of the riser, 9 m long. The crowd (blue) fills the floor from the barrier to under the crane.

The machinery stays the backdrop: the press (to 5.3 m) stands behind the right half of the riser and the machine line beside it further right, so from the floor the DJ is seen against the press; the goalpost header at 7 m is above the press's crown.

No stage deck, no towers: the DJ stand alone. Two 5 m arms of 290 mm square box truss (Global Truss F34 — src/rigbuild/pieces.js; Prolyte H30V is the same class but does not couple to F34: one system for the whole X) cross FLAT at a 4-way junction (Global Truss F34 SQ-4133 '4-way cross junction') under the bridge of the overhead crane parked over the DJ, one arm along the bridge, one across it pointing out over the crowd; bottom chord 5.96 m, on 4 climbing chain hoists, each on a two-leg bridle from the girders, a safety steel each, and two restraint steels at every arm end; load on the X ≈ 227 kg, on the crane ≈ 355 kg. rigging sign-off owed (crane rated load, lock-out, hoists + safety steels).

Strobes, blinders and hazers are other-supplier lines (the rental house lists none): each is a planning type modelled on a named product (scripts/place/fixtures/fixtures.json, EXT- codes). No CO2 jet, cold spark or confetti — the underground brief (versions file, method).

Each LOOK is one static state for previsualisation (a focus palette), not a show: positions are the rig's, aims and colours the look's. Every lamp but the press's own six mirrors about the nave centre line (x 0), the booth's axis too. Brightness between fixtures follows the datasheets (photometry below); the overall exposure is one chosen number (photometry.sceneScale).

junction.code: Global Truss F34 SQ-4133 '4-way cross junction'
junction.across_basis: legs 0.5 m from the centre — ESTIMATE: the maker's page gives the weight, not the leg length; the rental house's own junction may differ (then the straights change, not the X)

truss.section_class: 290 mm square box truss (Global Truss F34 — src/rigbuild/pieces.js; Prolyte H30V is the same class but does not couple to F34: one system for the whole X)
truss.trim_why: the shortest drop the rigging allows at the girder bottom the hall model carries (7.95 m measured, rail 8.1 m — audit A-01 2026-10-05; was 6.15 at the 8.15 m guess): a 90° bridle's apex hangs half its span under the flange — 1.1 m for the bridge-arm picks whose legs reach both girders (2.2 m apart) — then the climbing hoist's hook-to-suspension-plate minimum (≈0.50 m, read from the Chainmaster D8Plus 500 kg dimension sheet, p. 6) and ≈0.10 m of shackles: top chord 8.15 − 1.1 − 0.5 − 0.1 = 6.45 m, bottom chord 6.16 → 6.15 m. The crane rail is DISPUTED (6.6–8.4 m): at the low end every height here drops by 1.0 m (bottom chord ≈5.15 m, under the press crown 5.6 m, 0.1 m clear of it in plan) — measure the girder bottom on site before the trim is set.

motion.pendulum_L_basis: from the bridle anchors on the girder flange (8.15 m) to the hung mass's centre (the truss, 6.15–6.44 m, plus lamps standing 0.2–0.6 m above the top chord): 1.5–1.9 m. T = 2π√(L/g), g 9.81 m/s².
motion.restraint: each pick is a two-leg V bridle (the bridge-arm picks' V spans across the bridge, z; the crowd-arm picks' V spans along it, x), so the rigid X cannot translate either way without stretching a leg; two restraint steels at every arm end, up to the girders and spread in plan, stop it turning. What is left is the give of wire and slings: small, not zero.
rules: no pan or tilt move over the full range faster than 4 s (the heads' reaction torque is what pushes a hung truss)
no periodic movement (a chase, a sweep back and forth) with a period between 1.7 and 4 s — 0.7× to 1.5× the pendulum's 2.5–2.8 s — the band where a small push each cycle builds up
cue fades that move heads on the X are at least 4 s in the show's cue list
the crane locked out and isolated for the whole event (it is the rig's structure)

picks.bridle: two legs, one to a beam clamp on each girder's bottom flange (2.2 m apart), 90° between the legs, apex 1.1 m under the flange
right under a girder: two legs to beam clamps on that girder's flange 1.5 m apart along it, 90° between the legs, apex 0.75 m under the flange

tieoffs.what: at every arm end, two restraint steels up to beam clamps on the girders, spread in plan: the bridge arm's ends to both girders (a V across the bridge), the crowd and back ends to their own girder 1.5 m either side (a V along it). To the crane, not the floor: the crowd end hangs over people, where a floor anchor is a trip and crush point; the nave columns (≈11 m off) are the fallback for the bridge arm's ends.

rigging.signoff: rigging sign-off owed (crane rated load, lock-out, hoists + safety steels): the crane's rated load and a check of the old runway, rails and brakes; the crane locked in place and its power isolated for the whole event; the bridles' leg angles and the cantilevers (1.0 m on the bridge arm, 1.4 m on the crowd arm, beyond what the maker's span tables cover) calculated; a rigger's plan with point loads, signed by a structural or rigging engineer. This file draws it; they approve it.

effects.label: hazer
effects.note: 2 hazers on the floor behind the line, either side of the booth: the haze rolls from behind the DJ over the floor

budget.why: A browser cannot run ~90 real three.js spot lights: each is a term in the shader of every lit pixel and, with shadows on, a shadow render and a texture unit each (WebGL gives 16-32; past that every lit material fails to compile). Every fixture draws its beam cone; only these 8 lamps also light the room (the rest of the PARs' light on the columns and the press is baked, wash-glb.mjs), and shadows are OFF by default (the owner found the first version too laggy, 2026-09-27). Measured — see scripts/place/README.md, 'The rig'.
budget.realNote: 2026-09-28 (DJ place): the press's own uplights stand 0.35 m from it, where a real lamp in the renderer blows the face out white; they are baked like the other PARs, and the 4 header spots (6.3 m up, over the DJ and the press) are the real lamps that light the backdrop.

night.note: Darker than the base's readable night (ambient 0.8 -> 0.5, directional 0.35 -> 0.22): darkness is part of the design here (rule 1); the hall must still read in a render. Tuned by eye on the RTX 3080, 2026-09-28.

photometry.method: scripts/place/rig-lib.mjs, 'PHOTOMETRY': candela from the manifest (I = E*d^2 from a measured illuminance, else I = flux / beam solid angle); zoom keeps flux; three.js SpotLight intensity is candela x sceneScale; beam-in-air brightness ~ I*tan(theta/2), scaled to the brightest class, Stevens exponent 1/3, times `air`.
photometry.sceneScaleNote: ONE exposure number for the whole rig, chosen so the room reads in a browser's tone mapping (ACES, exposure 1). The ratios between fixtures are the datasheets'.
photometry.airNote: how much haze is in the air: the brightest class's beam gets this `haze` (0..1, src/objectComponents/spotBeam.js).
photometry.airWhy: Heavy haze (rule 4; 2-6 hazers in every version where the base had 4 smoke machines): every cone's air brightness at 1.5 where the base rig draws 0.9. A drawing choice, not photometry — the ratios between the fixtures stay the datasheets'.

white-cathedral.title: Four blades

one-beam.title: One blade
